tasks.title: Fix test project infrastructure
tasks.description:
The test project has two blocking issues that must be resolved before any real tests can run.

**1. ProjectReference path bug:** In `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests.csproj`, the path `../src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj` is wrong. From `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/`, `../` goes to `tests/` not the repo root. The correct path is `../../src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj`.

**2. TFM mismatch:** Tests target `net8.0` but only the .NET 10 runtime is available on this machine (`dotnet test` aborts with 'framework not found'). Change the test project TFM to `net10.0`.

**3. Add Moq and System.Net.Http:** Add `<PackageReference Include="Moq" Version="4.20.72" />` and `<PackageReference Include="System.Net.Http" Version="4.3.4" />` (or use the built-in HttpClient from net10.0 — just Moq is sufficient) so HTTP handler mocking is available for later tasks.

**4. Add InternalsVisibleTo:** In the driver project, add `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` containing `[assembly: System.Runtime.CompilerServices.InternalsVisibleTo("LinqPad.Databricks.Tests")]` so internal constructors on HTTP clients can be called from tests.

**Acceptance:** `dotnet build LinqPad.Databricks.sln` with 0 errors and 0 warnings; `dotnet test LinqPad.Databricks.sln` runs and passes all current smoke tests.

tasks.title: Implement Databricks HTTP base client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Http/DatabricksHttpClient.cs` — a reusable HTTP client wrapping `HttpClient` for all Databricks REST calls.

**Responsibilities:**
- Constructor `DatabricksHttpClient(string workspaceUrl, string pat)` — validates URL (regex `^https://[a-zA-Z0-9\-\.]+(\.(azuredatabricks\.net|databricks\.azure\.cn))/?$`), stores PAT.
- Internal/test constructor `DatabricksHttpClient(string workspaceUrl, string pat, HttpMessageHandler handler)` for injection of mock handlers.
- `GetAsync<T>(string path, CancellationToken ct)` and `PostAsync<T>(string path, object body, CancellationToken ct)` helpers: set `Authorization: Bearer <pat>` header, serialize/deserialize JSON with `System.Text.Json` (`JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true }`).
- On non-2xx response: read body, parse `{ "message": ... }` or `{ "error": ... }` field, throw a custom `DatabricksApiException(string message, string? errorCode, int statusCode)` that extends `Exception`.
- Expose `DatabricksApiException` as a public class in `Http/DatabricksApiException.cs`.

**JSON models needed now (add a `Models/` folder):**
- `PagedResponse<T>` with `Items: List<T>` and `NextPageToken: string?`.

**Acceptance:** Unit test with a `MockHttpMessageHandler` (manual `DelegatingHandler` subclass or Moq) can construct `DatabricksHttpClient` via the internal 3-arg constructor, perform a GET, and receive a deserialized object; also verify that a 4xx response throws `DatabricksApiException` with the parsed message.

tasks.title: Implement Unity Catalog REST client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Catalog/UnityCatalogClient.cs` using `DatabricksHttpClient`.

**Note:** `PagedResponse<T>` already exists at `Models/PagedResponse.cs` — do not recreate it.

**Models** (add to `Models/` or `Catalog/`):
- `CatalogInfo { string Name; string? Comment; }` — JSON property names: `name`, `comment`.
- `SchemaInfo { string Name; string CatalogName; string? Comment; }` — JSON: `name`, `catalog_name`, `comment`.
- `TableInfo { string Name; string SchemaName; string CatalogName; string TableType; string? Comment; }` — JSON: `name`, `schema_name`, `catalog_name`, `table_type`, `comment`. TableType values: `MANAGED`, `EXTERNAL`, `VIEW`, `MATERIALIZED_VIEW`.

API responses use `{ "catalogs": [...], "next_page_token": "..." }` for catalogs, `{ "schemas": [...] }` for schemas, `{ "tables": [...] }` for tables — NOT a generic `items` field. Model accordingly (separate paged-response wrappers or concrete response classes).

**Methods on `UnityCatalogClient`:**
- Constructor: `UnityCatalogClient(DatabricksHttpClient http)`.
- `ListCatalogsAsync(CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<CatalogInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/catalogs`, paginate via `next_page_token` by appending `?page_token={token}` on subsequent requests.
- `ListSchemasAsync(string catalogName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<SchemaInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/schemas?catalog_name={catalogName}`, paginate.
- `ListTablesAsync(string catalogName, string schemaName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<TableInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/tables?catalog_name={catalogName}&schema_name={schemaName}`, paginate.

**Acceptance:** Unit tests in `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/UnityCatalogClientTests.cs` using the existing `FakeHandler : DelegatingHandler` pattern: (a) `ListCatalogsAsync` single-page returns correct items; (b) multi-page (two responses with `next_page_token`) returns combined list; (c) `ListTablesAsync` passes both query params; (d) 403 response propagates as `DatabricksApiException`. `dotnet test` passes all tests.

tasks.title: Implement Statement Execution API client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Sql/StatementExecutionClient.cs` wrapping `DatabricksHttpClient`.

**Models** (add to `Models/` or `Sql/`):
- `StatementRequest`: `{ warehouse_id, statement, wait_timeout = "30s", on_wait_timeout = "CONTINUE", disposition = "INLINE", format = "JSON_ARRAY" }`.
- `StatementResponse`: `{ statement_id, status: { state, error? }, result? }` — model with nested classes.
- `StatementStatus`: `state` (string: PENDING, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED, CLOSED), `error?` (with `message`, `error_code`).
- `ResultSchema`: `{ columns: [ { name, type_name } ] }`.
- `ResultData`: `{ data_array: List<List<string?>> }` — inline chunk.
- `StatementResult`: `{ schema: ResultSchema, data_array?, next_chunk_index? }`.

**Method:**
`ExecuteAsync(string warehouseId, string sql, CancellationToken ct)` → `System.Data.DataTable`:
1. POST `/api/2.0/sql/statements` with `StatementRequest`.
2. If state is `PENDING` or `RUNNING`, poll `GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{statement_id}` every 500ms with exponential backoff capped at 2 seconds until terminal state.
3. On `FAILED`/`CANCELLED`/`CLOSED`, throw `DatabricksApiException(error.message, error.error_code, 0)`.
4. On `SUCCEEDED`, build a `DataTable`: columns from `result.schema.columns`, rows from `result.data_array` (all values as strings initially; cast to `double`/`long`/`bool` for obvious type_names like `DOUBLE`, `LONG`, `BOOLEAN`).
5. If `result.next_chunk_index` is present, fetch `GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{statement_id}/result/chunks/{chunk_index}` and append rows; repeat until no next chunk.

**Acceptance:** Unit tests in `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/StatementExecutionClientTests.cs` using the `FakeHandler` queue pattern: (a) immediate `SUCCEEDED` returns correct `DataTable` columns and rows; (b) `PENDING` then `SUCCEEDED` returns same result after polling; (c) `FAILED` throws `DatabricksApiException`; (d) two-chunk response produces combined rows. `dotnet test` passes.

tasks.title: Implement connection dialog (ShowConnectionDialog)
tasks.description:
Override `ShowConnectionDialog` in `DatabricksDriver.cs` using a WPF dialog loaded at runtime via reflection to avoid compile-time WPF SDK dependency on non-Windows builds.

**Implementation approach:** Load XAML string with `System.Windows.Markup.XamlReader.Parse(xaml)` and find controls with `System.Windows.LogicalTreeHelper.FindLogicalNode(root, name)`. Call all WPF types through reflection (Type.GetType, MethodInfo.Invoke) so the driver assembly does not need the WPF SDK at compile time.

**Dialog fields:**
- `WorkspaceUrl` (TextBox, required) — validate on OK against the same regex used by `DatabricksHttpClient`.
- `PersonalAccessToken` (PasswordBox or masked TextBox, required).
- `WarehouseId` (TextBox, required).
- `DefaultCatalog` (TextBox, optional).
- `DefaultSchema` (TextBox, optional).
- **Test Connection** button — instantiate `DatabricksHttpClient` + `UnityCatalogClient` using current field values, call `ListCatalogsAsync`, show inline status label with catalog count on success or error message on failure.
- OK / Cancel buttons.

**Persistence:**
- Read from `cxInfo.DriverData` (XElement) on open: populate fields from `WorkspaceUrl`, `WarehouseId`, `DefaultCatalog`, `DefaultSchema` child elements; decrypt PAT via `cxInfo.Decrypt(encryptedPat)`.
- On OK: write those four elements back; encrypt PAT via `cxInfo.Encrypt(pat)` and store as `EncryptedPat` element. Return `true`.
- On Cancel: do NOT mutate `DriverData`. Return `false`.

**Update `GetConnectionDescription`** to return `"{WorkspaceUrl} / {WarehouseId}"` if both are present.

**Acceptance:** `dotnet build` succeeds on Linux (no WPF SDK required). On Windows/LINQPad: dialog opens, fields pre-populate on edit, Test Connection shows feedback, Cancel leaves DriverData unchanged, OK persists encrypted PAT.

tasks.title: Implement Schema Explorer (GetSchemaAndBuildAssembly)
Implement ADO facade (IDbConnection/IDbCommand/IDataReader)
tasks.description:
Override `GetIDbConnection` in `DatabricksDriver` to return a custom `DbConnection` backed by the Statement Execution API, enabling LINQPad SQL mode.

**Classes to create** in `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Ado/`:

`DatabricksConnection : DbConnection`:
- Constructor: `DatabricksConnection(string workspaceUrl, string pat, string warehouseId)`.
- Stores a `StatementExecutionClient` (which holds a `DatabricksHttpClient`) internally.
- `ConnectionString` get/set — encode as `WorkspaceUrl={url};WarehouseId={id}` (PAT not in connection string).
- `Open()` / `Close()` / `OpenAsync()` — set `_state` field; REST is stateless so no actual network call needed in Open.
- `State` property returns `_state`.
- `CreateDbCommand()` returns a new `DatabricksCommand(this)`.
- Abstract members: `Database` returns empty string; `DataSource` returns workspace URL; `ServerVersion` returns `"0.0"`; `BeginDbTransaction` throws `NotSupportedException`; `ChangeDatabase` throws `NotSupportedException`.

`DatabricksCommand : DbCommand`:
- `CommandText` get/set.
- `ExecuteDbDataReader(CommandBehavior)` → calls `_connection.ExecutionClient.ExecuteAsync(warehouseId, CommandText, ct).GetAwaiter().GetResult()` and returns `dataTable.CreateDataReader()`.
- `ExecuteNonQuery()` → calls `ExecuteAsync`, returns `dataTable.Rows.Count`.
- `ExecuteScalar()` → calls `ExecuteAsync`, returns `dataTable.Rows.Count > 0 ? dataTable.Rows[0][0] : null`.
- Other abstract members: `Cancel()` no-op; `CreateDbParameter()` returns a `DatabricksParameter : DbParameter` stub; `Parameters` returns empty collection; `Prepare()` no-op; `Transaction` get/set (ignored); `UpdatedRowSource` get/set (ignored).

**Override in `DatabricksDriver`:**
```csharp
public override IDbConnection GetIDbConnection(IConnectionInfo cxInfo) {
    var url = cxInfo.DriverData.Element("WorkspaceUrl")?.Value ?? "";
    var pat = cxInfo.Decrypt(cxInfo.DriverData.Element("EncryptedPat")?.Value ?? "");
    var wh = cxInfo.DriverData.Element("WarehouseId")?.Value ?? "";
    var conn = new DatabricksConnection(url, pat, wh);
    conn.Open();
    return conn;
}
```

**Acceptance:** `dotnet build` succeeds. In LINQPad SQL mode, `SELECT 1` executes and returns a result. Exceptions from the API surface with meaningful messages.

tasks.title: Expand unit tests for UC and SE clients
tasks.description:
Add meaningful unit tests covering the UC and Statement Execution clients. The existing `DatabricksHttpClientTests.cs` already has 2 tests covering HTTP GET success and 4xx error — do NOT replace those. Smoke test files (`DatabricksTests.cs`, `DriverStubTests.cs`) can remain.

**Add `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/UnityCatalogClientTests.cs`:**
- Use the same `FakeHandler : DelegatingHandler` pattern from `DatabricksHttpClientTests.cs`, or create a `QueuedFakeHandler` that dequeues responses in order.
- `ListCatalogsAsync_SinglePage_ReturnsItems`: mock one response with `{ "catalogs": [{"name":"cat1"}] }`, assert 1 item with `Name=="cat1"`.
- `ListCatalogsAsync_MultiPage_CombinesResults`: mock two responses (first has `next_page_token`, second does not), assert combined count.
- `ListTablesAsync_PassesQueryParams`: capture the request URL in the handler, assert `catalog_name` and `schema_name` are present.
- `ListCatalogsAsync_ApiError_ThrowsDatabricksApiException`: 403 response → `DatabricksApiException`.

**Add `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/StatementExecutionClientTests.cs`:**
- `ExecuteAsync_ImmediateSucceeded_ReturnsDataTable`: POST response is `SUCCEEDED` with `schema` and `data_array`; assert column names and row values.
- `ExecuteAsync_PendingThenSucceeded_Polls`: first response is `PENDING`, second is `SUCCEEDED`; assert correct `DataTable`.
- `ExecuteAsync_FailedState_ThrowsDatabricksApiException`: response state `FAILED` with error message; assert exception message.
- `ExecuteAsync_MultiChunk_CombinesRows`: first result has `next_chunk_index=1`, second GET returns additional rows; assert total row count.

**Acceptance:** `dotnet test LinqPad.Databricks.sln` reports all tests passing (0 failures, 0 skipped). No `Thread.Sleep` in tests.

tasks.title: Add NuGet metadata and finalize packaging
tasks.description:
The `publish.sh` and `publish.ps1` scripts already exist and produce `.LPX6` and `.nupkg`. The driver csproj currently lacks NuGet metadata.

**Add to `LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj` `<PropertyGroup>`:**
```xml
<GeneratePackageOnBuild>false</GeneratePackageOnBuild>
<PackageId>LinqPad.Databricks.Driver</PackageId>
<Version>0.1.0</Version>
<Authors>hpractv</Authors>
<Description>Azure Databricks Data Context Driver for LINQPad 8+. Connects via Unity Catalog REST API and SQL Statement Execution API.</Description>
<PackageTags>linqpaddriver databricks azure unity-catalog</PackageTags>
<RepositoryUrl>https://github.com/hpractv/linqpad-databricks-connector</RepositoryUrl>
<PackageReadmeFile>README.md</PackageReadmeFile>
```
Also add an `<ItemGroup>` with `<None Include="../../README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath="/" />`.

**NuGet lib TFM for macOS compatibility:** Per the epic plan, the NuGet `lib/` folder should use `net8.0` (not `net8.0-windows`) so the package is visible on macOS. Easiest approach: use a `.nuspec` file or override the `PackageTfm`. Alternatively, document this as a known limitation in `README.md` for phase 1 (Windows-only).

**Post-build dev copy target:** The csproj already has a `CopyToLinqPad` target for Windows. Verify the target directory name (`DatabricksDriver`) matches the expected LINQPad driver folder naming convention from the docs.

**Validate:** Run `./publish.sh Release 0.1.0` and confirm `dist/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.0.1.0.LPX6` and `dist/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.0.1.0.nupkg` are produced. Inspect with `unzip -l` and confirm `linqpaddriver` is in the tags and the lib path is correct.
